text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A Syrian official source says: accusations of Syria sponsoring terrorism are false.. U.S. move to block arms deal between South Africa and Syria will damage U.S. credibility.
- South Africa's President Nelson Mandela rejects U.S. warning over arms deal with Syria.
- Luxembourg foreign minister Jacques Poos says Europe extremely interested in Middle East peace.
- More Israeli oppression in Golan and two youths arrested.

- Israel and Palestinian Authority sign deal on Israeli redeployment in West Bank town of Hebron. U.S. guarantees allow Israel to choose areas it wants to control. Palestinians denounce concessions made by the Palestinan Authority over the deal.
- Lebanese President Elias Hrawi describes Hebron deal as an instrument to pressure Syria and Lebanon.
- Syrian cabinet allocates $24.5 million to finance some imports.
- Cooperation agreement between Syria and the Jordanian Islamic Action Front calls for solidarity and support for Syria to counter dangers facing the Arab nation.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak says: "Syria rejected an Israeli offer to negotiate with Damascus first then Lebanon."
- Lebanese resistance units destroy Israeli position in south Lebanon.
